head.title: Business Lunch Catering Dubai | From AED 90 Per Head
head.meta_description: Business lunch catering in Dubai from AED 90 per head delivered, AED 120-150 for a buffet, AED 700-950 for a chef cooking in the room. Real per-head rates, published.
head.h1: Business Lunch Catering in Dubai — Per-Head Prices From AED 90

opening_paragraph: Business lunch catering in Dubai starts at AED 90 per head for a delivered working lunch. A buffet set up in your room starts at AED 120 per head, a premium spread with a live station or canapés at AED 150, and a chef who cooks and serves in front of your guests runs AED 700–950 per head. Add 5% VAT to all four.
Send the date, the headcount and the floor you sit on. An itemised quote comes back the same working day, with food, staff, delivery and equipment on separate lines.

replace_in_block.new_heading: Cheap business lunch catering in Dubai, honestly
new_paragraphs: People search for cheap business lunch catering in Dubai and they are right to. Feeding a project team through a long programme is a real line item, and the gap between AED 90 and AED 150 a head across a year is a hire.

What we will not do is pretend AED 90 is the floor of the market, because it is not. You can order lower than that, and below it something has been taken out: the protein shrinks, the delivery window turns into a suggestion, or nobody turns up to set the food out and your office manager ends up doing it. We price from AED 90 because that is where the kitchen can send food we would eat at our own desks. If your budget sits firmly underneath, a platter order from a sandwich shop will serve you better, and we would rather say so now than at the quote.
How much does business lunch catering cost in Dubai?

A delivered working lunch starts at AED 90 per head. A business lunch buffet set up in your room starts at AED 120 per head. A premium buffet, live station or canapé spread starts at AED 150 per head. A private chef cooking and serving in the room is AED 700–950 per head. Add 5% VAT to every figure.
What does business lunch mean in Dubai?

A business lunch is a working meal built around a meeting rather than around the food. In Dubai the phrase covers two different purchases: a restaurant's fixed-price set menu served during the working day, and catering brought into your own office or meeting room. This page prices the second one.
Is there a minimum headcount or minimum order for a business lunch?

Yes, and here they are. A delivered working lunch starts at 10 guests, a buffet at 20 guests, and every order has a minimum value of AED 900. A chef cooking and serving in the room carries no minimum headcount, because that format is priced per head from AED 700 and works for a table of two. Most Dubai caterers publish neither figure, so ask every shortlisted company for both before you compare quotes.
What is the difference between office lunch delivery and staffed service?

Office lunch delivery means the food arrives ready, gets laid out on your boardroom table, and your team clears it. That is the AED 90 tier. Staffed service means our team builds the line, holds the food at temperature, serves, then clears and wipes down. That is where the AED 120 and AED 150 tiers sit, because you are paying for people and equipment as well as food.
Can you cater a business lunch for a small team of six?

Yes, against the minimums. Small business lunch catering runs as a delivered drop-off rather than a staffed buffet, because putting two service staff behind a line for six guests costs more than the food does. The per-head rate still starts at AED 90, and the order is quoted against the 10-guest, AED 900 floor, which for six people usually buys a better menu rather than more trays. A chef cooking in the room has no minimum headcount at all.
Is cheap business lunch catering in Dubai worth it?

Below roughly AED 90 per head in this market something has been removed: the protein shrinks, the delivery window becomes a suggestion, or nobody arrives to set the food out. We price from AED 90 because that is where we can send food we would eat at our own desks. If your budget sits firmly under that, a sandwich platter order will serve you better.
Do you run business lunch deals or set-price packages?

No. Business lunch deals in Dubai are a restaurant format, where a venue sells a fixed-price two or three course menu at midday. We publish per-head bands instead, starting at AED 90, and quote your exact headcount and format against them. There is no published discount table for volume and no membership rate.
How do I judge the top 10 catering companies in Dubai lists?

Most of those lists are written by caterers who appear on them, so treat them as a source of names and nothing more. The best way to compare catering services in Dubai is to send the same brief to five of them and ask for the per-head rate, the minimum order, whether staff and delivery sit inside that rate, the notice period, and whether VAT is in the number shown.
How much notice do you need, and can I change the headcount?

We publish no fixed minimum notice, so ask about the date you want rather than assuming it is too soon. We typically reply within 15 minutes during business hours on whether a chef and kitchen are free, and an itemised proposal follows within one business day. Headcounts move, so tell us as early as you can and we will confirm in writing the last point at which the kitchen can still change the order.
Do you cover dietary requirements at a business lunch?
Every business lunch menu can be built halal, vegetarian, vegan, gluten-free, dairy-free, keto or nut-free, with allergens labelled on each dish so guests choose without asking.
Send your headcount and get an itemised quote or message us on WhatsApp .

We cover business districts across the city: DIFC, Downtown and Business Bay, out to Dubai Marina, JLT, Media City, Internet City, Dubai South and the Jebel Ali business parks. Chefs and delivery teams sit across those areas so food arrives at temperature instead of after a long crawl down Sheikh Zayed Road. Lift access, parking and load-in get agreed with your reception team before the first delivery, then fixed for the rest of the programme. Explore conference catering , corporate catering , the wider catering in Dubai range, or price a room with our catering cost calculator .

add_block.new_heading: How much does business lunch catering cost in Dubai?
new_paragraphs: Here is the whole rate card, with nothing behind a form.
What you are buying Service level Per head
Working lunch for a meeting or project room Delivered, laid out, your team clears From AED 90
Business lunch buffet for a bigger session Delivered and set up; staff optional From AED 120
Premium buffet, live station or canapés Staffed on site through the service From AED 150
Chef cooking and serving your lunch on site Chef plus service team, plated to the agenda AED 700–950

Two things move the number inside each band: how much labour the format needs, and how far the food travels. Ten people at a boardroom table and ninety at a town hall pay different rates for the same dish, because the cost of a chef and a van spreads differently across the room. VAT at 5% sits on top of every figure, the standard rate published by the UAE Federal Tax Authority .

Printing these bands at all is unusual in this city. Most catering services in Dubai that outrank this page show no per-head figure anywhere on their own site, including two of the largest catering companies in the corporate space, who quote on request only. You cannot compare rates nobody prints, which is the whole reason ours sit on the page.

add_block.new_heading: Office lunch delivery or staffed service
new_paragraphs: This choice sets your budget, so settle it before you shortlist anyone.

Office lunch delivery in Dubai. Food arrives hot or chilled as the dish needs it, in sealed single portions or on shared platters, with tongs, napkins and allergen labels. We lay it out on the boardroom table or the kitchen counter and your team helps itself. This is the AED 90 tier, and it covers most weekday office lunch catering.

Staffed service. Our team arrives ahead of the sitting, builds the line with chafing dishes and linen, holds hot food hot and cold food cold, replenishes through the break, then clears and wipes down so the room is usable for the next meeting. The AED 120 and AED 150 tiers sit here.

A chef cooking in the room. Cooking and plating happen in front of your guests, with courses timed to the agenda so nobody is caught mid-bite when the discussion turns. That is the AED 700–950 band, priced for a signing lunch or a client hosting day rather than for feeding the floor on a Tuesday.
If a quote does not say which of those three you are getting, it is not a quote yet. Our drop-off catering and buffet catering pages break each format down further.

add_block.new_heading: Business lunch catering ideas that survive a meeting room
new_paragraphs: The menu gets built to your table rather than pulled off a shelf, and the business lunch catering ideas that work all share one trait: they hold at room temperature and stay clean to eat one-handed.
Composed salads and grain bowls — quinoa, roast vegetable and herb bowls that do not wilt across a two-hour session.
Levantine mezze — hummus, moutabel, fattoush, vine leaves and warm flatbread, laid down the middle of the table to share.
Grilled proteins — chicken shish, sea bass, lamb kofta or a vegetarian equivalent, portioned so nobody queues.
Modern European plates for client-facing lunches, where the room wants a course rather than a platter.
Sealed individual boxes for staggered sittings, hybrid teams and anyone eating at a desk between calls.
A light finish — cut fruit, a small dessert selection, and coffee that lands when the break does.

Every dish can be built halal, vegetarian, vegan, gluten-free, dairy-free, keto or nut-free, with allergens labelled on the dish itself so guests choose without asking. Full options sit on our menus page.

add_block.new_heading: Small teams, small offices and small party catering
new_paragraphs: Small business lunch catering gets quoted honestly here rather than turned away. The delivered working lunch starts at 10 guests and every order has to reach AED 900, so a table of six is still fed — the quote simply prices against that floor. Under roughly fifteen guests we run it as a drop-off rather than a staffed line, because two service staff behind a buffet for six people costs more than the food does and you would be paying for theatre. The per-head rate still starts at AED 90.

A buffet needs 20 guests before we will build one, above about twenty-five a staffed line starts earning its cost, and past sixty you want one, because a queue that moves badly ruins a lunch break faster than average food does. The same logic covers small party catering in Dubai when the reason to eat is a leaving lunch or a quarter-end win rather than a working meeting.

add_block.new_heading: Business lunch deals in Dubai, and why we do not run one
new_paragraphs: Search for business lunch deals in Dubai and you mostly get restaurants selling a fixed-price midday set menu, often two or three courses at a flat rate per person. That is a good buy when you are hosting one or two clients and want a table booked in DIFC.

Catering works differently, so we publish bands instead of a deal. There is no discount table for volume, no membership rate, and no seasonal offer that expires on Thursday. What you get is the same AED 90, AED 120 and AED 150 starting points whoever is asking, then an itemised quote against your real headcount. If a caterer waves a headline deal at you, check what the food, the staff and the delivery each cost inside it before you compare.

add_block.new_heading: How to judge the top 10 catering companies in Dubai lists
new_paragraphs: Search that phrase and you get rankings written by caterers who appear on them. Take the names, ignore the order, then put a shortlist of five through the same five questions. The best way to compare is in writing, side by side.
What is the per-head rate for my exact format? Not a range for the whole business, the number for a delivered lunch for my headcount.
Is there a minimum order value or minimum headcount? Several Dubai caterers hold a minimum order in the several-hundred-dirham range, which changes everything for a team of eight.
Are service staff, delivery, setup and equipment inside that rate? This is the single biggest cause of a quote landing higher than the number you were shown.
What notice do you need, and what is the cut-off to change numbers? Headcounts move on the morning of the meeting.
Is VAT in the figure shown? 5% across a year of weekly lunches is not a rounding error.
Run our quote through the same five. If another company answers them better, take the other company.

add_block.new_heading: What we can prove, and what we cannot
new_paragraphs: The sites ranking around this page carry client logo walls, star ratings and accreditation badges. Here is our position on both halves of that, in plain terms.

True and checkable: the chefs and partner kitchens handling your lunch work to Dubai Municipality food-safety requirements , and trade-licence details go out with the quote whenever you ask. No chef is offered corporate work before clearing identity checks, a practical cooking assessment, reference verification and ongoing performance review, which is set out on how we vet our chefs . MyCHEF is part of Global Catering, operating since 2015.

Not on this page: client logos, star ratings, quotes from named companies, and badges. We hold no written permission from the offices we have cooked for to publish their names, and we will not display a mark we cannot hand you the paperwork for. When that permission exists it goes here with the client named. Until then you have the published rate card, an itemised quote, on the booking, and the anonymised briefs in our.
